title: When in the Light of Faith Divine
description: When in the Light of Faith Divine in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 101, headed “The world's three great temptations”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When in the light of faith di-vine We look on things be-low, Hon-our, and gold, and sen-sual joy, How vain and dan-gerous too!

lines: When in the light of faith divine
Honour, and gold, and sensual joy,
Honour's a puff of noisy breath;
Whilst others starve the nobler mind,
They rob the serpent of his food
The pleasures that allure our sense
There's but a drop of flattering sweet,
In him my vast desires are fill'd,
In vain the world accosts my ear,
I cannot buy your bliss so dear,
Nor part with heaven for you.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
